finding.claim: OS command injection in /ping: the unauthenticated query parameter `host` is concatenated into a shell command string passed to child_process.exec, so shell metacharacters (; | && $() backticks) execute arbitrary commands as the server user. The route has no authentication.
finding.source: req.query.host (HTTP GET /ping?host=...), any unauthenticated remote client
finding.sink: child_process.exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host) at tools.js:7, which spawns a shell; output returned in the response at tools.js:11

trace.note: GET /ping handler registered with no auth middleware
req.query.host concatenated unsanitized into shell command passed to exec
command stdout returned to attacker, so output is directly exfiltrated

finding.guards_checked: No validation, allowlist, or escaping of host; no authentication or middleware; no use of execFile with an argument array (execFile is used only in /version, which is not attacker-influenced). Express can also deliver arrays/objects for req.query.host, but string concatenation still yields injection. Example payload: /ping?host=127.0.0.1;id

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host straight to shell-spawning exec in the unauthenticated GET /ping handler (tools.js:6), with no auth, validation or middleware anywhere (app.listen at tools.js:28), and stdout is returned at tools.js:11 (e.g. host=127.0.0.1;id exits 0 so the output is sent).
